concept.name: Inflation
concept.definition: A sustained increase in the general level of prices for goods and services over time, equivalently a decline in the purchasing power of money. In the U.S. it is most commonly measured by the 12-month percent change in the Consumer Price Index or the PCE price index.
concept.intuition: Inflation means your dollar buys less this year than last year; central banks target a low, stable rate (the Fed aims for 2%) because both very high inflation and deflation damage the economy.
concept.mechanics: Statistical agencies track a fixed basket of consumer goods and services and compute the average price change over time; the 12-month percent change of the index is the headline inflation rate. Persistent inflation is ultimately associated with money supply growing faster than output, though shocks (energy, supply chains) drive short-run swings.
concept.formula: Inflation rate (12-month) = (CPI_t / CPI_{t-12} - 1) x 100, where CPI_t is the consumer price index in month t.
concept.failure_modes: Headline rates are dominated by volatile food and energy swings; substitution, quality change, and housing measurement make any single index an approximation, and base effects can make year-over-year rates jump mechanically.
concept.misconceptions: A fall in the inflation rate does not mean prices are falling (that is deflation) — it means prices are rising more slowly; also, one expensive item is not inflation, which refers to the general price level.
concept.example: U.S. CPI inflation peaked at 9.1% year-over-year in June 2022, prompting the Federal Reserve's 2022-2023 rate-hiking cycle.

citations.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Consumer Price Index (CPI Home)
